portable_question: Store app data in a portable .\data folder? (Choose No to use your Windows profile)
nvidia_missing: No NVIDIA GPU was detected; managed llama.cpp will use the CPU backend.
cuda_detected: NVIDIA GPU and CUDA Toolkit detected; managed llama.cpp will use CUDA.
cuda_missing: An NVIDIA GPU was detected, but the CUDA Toolkit compiler is not installed.
cuda_benefit: CUDA moves model inference to a supported NVIDIA GPU and is usually much faster than CPU. Managed llama.cpp source builds also require the CUDA Toolkit.
cuda_tradeoff: CUDA uses several GB of disk plus GPU memory and needs a compatible NVIDIA driver. CPU avoids those requirements but is much slower for larger models.
cuda_question: Select CUDA and install the Toolkit?
setup_llm_question: Set up local LLM providers for chat?
llama_benefit: Managed llama.cpp is preferred when you want MagicHandy to own a pinned, tuned runner with predictable startup, model loading, structured replies, and diagnostics.
llama_ollama_tradeoff: Ollama is simpler when already installed and saves compiler/runtime disk space, but MagicHandy has less control over its runner version and launch settings.
ollama_additional_question: Install or keep Ollama as an additional provider?
ollama_model_optional: Optional Ollama model to ensure now (blank leaves models unchanged)
parakeet_benefit: Parakeet adds private offline speech recognition: 1.4 MB CPU runner plus a 644 MiB CC-BY-4.0 model.
tts_benefit: A managed local TTS module can speak chat replies privately without a cloud API.
tts_zero_dependencies: No Python, uv, PyTorch, or compiler needs to be preinstalled; the selected module receives an isolated managed environment.
tts_storage_tradeoff: Local TTS downloads several GiB and may share GPU memory with the LLM. Choosing No leaves existing TTS settings and assets unchanged.
tts_question: Install or keep a local text-to-speech module through this installer?
tts_faster_benefit: Faster Qwen3-TTS is the preferred NVIDIA path for cloning quality and latency; it requires CUDA, a reference WAV, and its exact transcript.
tts_chatterbox_benefit: Chatterbox is the broader fallback and works on CPU or NVIDIA; CPU avoids VRAM use but generates speech more slowly.
tts_option_faster: Faster Qwen3-TTS (NVIDIA CUDA; reference voice required)
tts_option_chatterbox: Chatterbox Turbo (CPU or NVIDIA; bundled voice available)
tts_module_invalid: Choose 1 for Faster Qwen3-TTS or 2 for Chatterbox.
tts_faster_unavailable: Faster Qwen3-TTS requires a working NVIDIA driver and GPU. Choose Chatterbox CPU on this machine.
tts_faster_cuda_only: Faster Qwen3-TTS cannot use CPU; select TTSDevice cuda or choose Chatterbox.
tts_cuda_benefit: CUDA makes Chatterbox substantially faster on a supported NVIDIA GPU. CPU saves GPU memory for the LLM.
tts_cuda_unavailable: CUDA TTS was selected, but no working NVIDIA driver and GPU were detected.
tts_auto_launch_benefit: Auto-launch lets MagicHandy own the local server lifecycle; turn it off only when you plan to run the server yourself.
tts_auto_launch_question: Launch the selected TTS server with MagicHandy?
tts_reference_unattended: Unattended Faster Qwen3-TTS setup requires TTSReferenceWav and TTSReferenceTranscript.
tts_reuse: The installed TTS module is valid and will be reused without another multi-gigabyte install.
ollama_forced: Ollama remains enabled because no managed llama.cpp runtime was selected.
parakeet_keep_question: Install or keep managed Parakeet speech input?
